Detroit is a 3.5-point favorite in the latest Lions vs. Panthers odds from DraftKings Sportsbook, and the Over/Under on the game total is set at 47.5 points. They also placed both starting cornerbacks on IR, so things could be dicey against this explosive Lions offense. The Lions' last appearance in prime time cashed everyone out with the explosive matchup against the Bills . I'm not expecting Carolina to perform like Buffalo did, but the Panthers are highly susceptible to being dragged into shootouts if their opponent starts to sling the ball around. Given the dearth of defensive backfield talent out there for Carolina, I fully expect the Lions to take advantage and throw the ball downfield. Carolina should be able to answer and we should get points galore. He broke out in Week 2 with a pair of scores then was rewarded with eight targets in Week 3 against the Browns . I'd expect him to see close to that many again Sunday night, making this number just way too low for how much Bryce looks his way, especially if Jalen Coker ends up inactive tonight. Jahmyr Gibbs Over 37.5 receiving yards (-115, DraftKings) Gibbs is the unquestioned best running back in football right now and has really rewarded anyone who took him first overall in fantasy. But he's not just a great runner, he's also an elite receiver, and in a game that should be a shootout with Jared Goff looking to exploit the Panthers defense, I'd expect Gibbs to be plenty involved in the pass game as well. 40 receiving yards feels very, very doable for the superstar. Bet on NFL player props and more at BetMGM: Sunday Night Football anytime touchdowns Jameson Williams (+200, DraftKings) If Williams wasn't having such a meh year so far, this number wouldn't be north of 2-1. But he's been just OK thus far, and as such we're getting a great price. Jamo can score from anywhere, should get plenty of short-yardage looks with screens and the like and also is the ultimate deep threat going against a really depleted secondary. Brycen Tremayne (+360, DraftKings) This is a bit of a longshot, but, again, we're thinking Jalen Coker won't play in this game. That's going to likely slide Tremayne into a starting role opposite of Tetairoa McMillan at wide receiver, and if this is a shootout, Young is going to have to throw a lot. There's a good chance Tremayne gets lost in the sauce near the end zone, setting him up as a nice high-value play to score. By Zachary Cohen - October 3, 2026 87472 X Facebook Email It’s time for Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season. I strongly suggest you check out the Week 4 NFL Betting Hub , where you’ll find all of the features and picks from my talented co-workers. On top of that, we never stop pumping out good NFL content on our live shows . That’s the beauty of being a subscriber. As a company, we’re relentless in our effort to get you prepared for these games. With that out of the way, let’s get into the fun stuff. Keep reading for my Week 4 NFL best bets and Week 4 NFL player props. MORE: Check out our Pro Picks page for NFL best bets from all of our analysts Indianapolis Colts vs. Washington Commanders – 9:30 am ET (London) The Colts might be down Alec Pierce, but I like the way this offense operates. Indianapolis lost a tough one in Kansas City two weeks ago, but the team put up 30 points against a Chiefs team that is sixth in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (-0.077) this year. It’s just hard to stop the Colts once Jonathan Taylor gets going on the ground. He puts Indianapolis in a ton of manageable third-and-short situations. Of course, Washington is a top-five team in Rush EPA/Play Allowed (-0.318) right now. The Commanders have done a good job of stuffing opponents thus far. But they haven’t seen an offensive line quite like this, and they haven’t faced a running back this efficient. Also, if Washington is selling out to stop the run, Daniel Jones should be able to do some real damage through the air — especially when looking Josh Downs’ way. I also happen to love the Commanders to put up points on the Colts defense. Marcus Mariota is an excellent backup, so Washington’s offense isn’t going to completely stall out with Jayden Daniels injured. Mariota played well in relief of Daniels two games ago, and he threw for three touchdowns in his start last week. He’s accurate, he understands the offense, and he’s still a threat with his legs. He’s also up against a Colts defense that is 30th in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (0.124). Honestly, this might not seem like the most enticing standalone game, but I think it’s going to deliver some early-morning excitement. Two shaky defenses should mean a real shot at a shootout. Also, since 2024, the Over is 15-1 when Washington is an underdog of 3.5 to 9.5 points. The average total points scored in such games is 58.2 points per game. Bet: Over 46.5 (-115) Dallas Cowboys at Houston Texans – 1:00 pm ET We haven’t seen anything from Houston this season, but a bounce-back performance should be coming soon. I don’t expect the Texans to completely stifle a good Cowboys offense, but I do know that Houston is much better than its No. 19 ranking in EPA/Play Allowed (0.012) this year. This is a Texans defense that has been elite for years, and none of the moves made in the offseason should have resulted in this type of drop-off. That said, look for Houston to start playing some much better defense, and we could see it start with a decent showing against Dak Prescott and Co. I also love any offense in a matchup with the Cowboys defense, as Dallas is at the bottom of the league in EPA/Play Allowed (0.193). The Cowboys made some moves to address their miserable defense from last season, but it doesn’t look like any of them have worked. So, this should be a pretty strong matchup for CJ Stroud. Of course, Stroud has issues as a passer, but he’s reliable when he has time to get his feet set. That’s a good thing as Stroud prepares to face a defense that is 31st in Pass Rush Win Rate (40%). He should have plenty of time. This is also a massive desperation spot for Houston. I can’t imagine Dallas is thrilled to be sitting at 1-2 right now, but Houston’s season might be over if the team drops this one to fall to 0-4. Bet: Texans ML (-136) Arizona Cardinals at New York Giants – 1:00 pm ET Jameis Winston has been pretty buttoned up since taking over for Jaxson Dart, but I imagine he’ll be slinging it around a bit here. This season, the Cardinals are allowing 247.0 passing yards per game, and their two starting corners have an average PFF grade of 52.1. New York has been conservative with Winston so far, opting to lean heavily into a ground-and-pound approach. However, the Giants need to play the matchup, and this is one that calls for some passing. Arizona is a top-10 team in pass frequency. So, if the Cardinals are letting Jacoby Brissett air it out, the Giants will have no choice but to let Winston do the same. I know Winston hasn’t yet thrown for a score, and he also hasn’t eclipsed 118 passing yards in a game. But we all know that Winston is a gunslinger, and you don’t have to go back too far to find a box score in which he threw for 366 yards and two touchdowns. That was November 23, 2025, when Winston got involved in a shootout with the Lions. Steelers @ Browns Pittsburgh coach Mike McCarthy said he wanted to push the ball down the field more this year than the team did last year with Aaron Rodgers, and he has been true to his word so far. Rodgers’ average depth of target has been over 10 yards in two of the three games so far, including in a 30-27 win last week. I’ll go over the 38.5, as the Steelers take on a Browns team with some interesting young weapons and an underrated offense. Hill's Pick: Over 38.5 Colts @ Commanders Don’t forget to set your alarms for this one, as we get our first 9:30 am ET kickoff of the season in London come Sunday. Both teams started 0-2 before winning in Week 3. With the winner getting to .500, I’ll take the 3.5 with the Commanders in what should be a close game. Hill's Pick: Commanders +3.5 Patriots @ Bills It has not been pretty for the defending AFC champions, but it’s often a good idea to ignore the last thing you saw in the NFL to avoid overreacting. The Patriots will already be 3.5 games out of first place in the AFC East with a loss. They are desperate and getting 6.5 points. I’l bet on them to bounce back. Hill's Pick: Patriots +6.5 Titans @ Ravens If the Titans aren’t the worst team in the NFL, they’re pretty close to it. At 0-3, their offense has been anemic, and I don’t expect it to improve this week in Baltimore. Hill's Pick: Titans Under 15.5 Jaguars @ Bengals The quarterbacks for this game are familiar with each other. Trevor Lawrence and Joe Burrow were picked first overall, respectively, in back-to-back years (2020 and 2021), and also played against each other in the 2019 college football national title game. The Jaguars look like a contender and could easily be 3-0. In a toss-up game, I’ll take the points. Hill's Pick: Jaguars +2.5 Rams @ Eagles Panic time could officially hit the Rams if they lose again this week and fall to 1-3. The Eagles have had their number recently, winning all four meetings since the start of the 2023 season, and winning in Philadelphia isn’t easy, especially considering the onerous travel the Rams have endured already this season. Hill's Pick: Eagles +3 Cardinals @ Giants The Giants are 2-1, but their offense has looked suspect since quarterback Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending knee injury. With the total set at 44.5, I think we get a 23-20 type of game. I will go Under here considering the Giants' lackluster offense. Hill's Pick: Under 44.5 Cowboys @ Texans The Cowboys’ defense was expected to be improved in 2026 after being dreadful in 2025, but we have yet to see that play out. The Cowboys' elite offense and shaky defense make them a good Over team until proven otherwise. Hill's Pick: Over 48.5 Jets @ Bears The Jets lost and failed to cover last week vs. the Lions, but were tied with just a few minutes to go. Quarterback Geno Smith has played very well for the Jets, and I think they will keep it close this week against the Bears. Hill's Pick: Jets +3.5 Packers @ Buccaneers Two desperate teams facing off here with each in dire need of a win. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels will make his first career start for the Buccaneers, and I expect points to be hard to come by. Hill's Pick: Under 38.5 Dolphins @ Vikings The Vikings look to improve to 4-0 and are heavy favorites to do so against the hapless Dolphins. Star wide receiver Justin Jefferson might be sidelined for this one, and 10.5 points is a lot to lay for a struggling Vikings offense. Hill's Pick: Dolphins +10.5 Chiefs @ Raiders Raiders’ tight end Brock Bowers is one of the best, and perhaps, still one of the most underrated players in the league. I don’t look for them to do much offensively on the road, in a hostile environment against an angry Seahawks defense coming off an upset loss to the Commanders. Hill's Pick: Chargers Under 17.5 Broncos @ 49ers The 49ers are undefeated and have been ultra impressive so far, but as usual, the injuries are starting to pile up. In what should be a close game, I’ll take the Broncos to keep it close. Hill's Pick: Broncos +3 Lions @ Panthers The Lions have played three games and they’ve all gone Over. With an elite offense and very suspect defense, I like another Lions Over. Hill's Pick: Over 51.5 Falcons @ Saints The Saints gave up over 100 yards rushing last week and now face perhaps the most dynamic running back in the NFL. Look for Bijan Robinson to have another big game on the ground. NFL Draft predictions to target Ravens draft offensive lineman first (+130) The offensive line was a major issue for Baltimore last year, and it hasn't gotten any better with Tyler Linderbaum leaving for Las Vegas. Whether it's moving up a bit for Francis Mauigoa or Spencer Fano, taking a plug-and-play interior lineman like Olaivavega Ioane, or even selecting Kadyn Proctor as the heir apparent at left tackle, the Ravens should be using a draft like this that isn't considered stacked with blue-chip talent to stock up on help to address their biggest weakness. Carnell Tate draft position: Under 7.5 (-105) The market appears to be predicting a little bit of a slide for Tate after the Ohio State receiver was once considered the clear option for the Browns at No. 6. While I believe Cleveland will go with an offensive lineman at that spot, I don't know that Tate gets by the Commanders at No. 7, particularly if Jeremiyah Love and Sonny Styles go off the board in the top five. Tate would be a great running mate and eventual replacement for Terry McLaurin, and receiver is a clear need for Washington. Getting the underdog side of this market while having the potential to hit with either the Browns or Commanders seems like good value. Rueben Bain drafted before Mansoor Delane (-120) This is a head-to-head matchup available at DraftKings that I could see shifting quickly. Teams don't seem to be too worried about Bain's arm length, and on ability alone he has an argument to be taken in the top five in the same tier as Arvell Reese and David Bailey. Delane is probably the best corner prospect in the draft, though a team comfortable with Jermod McCoy's medicals could prefer him, and there is good enough depth at corner that I don't see Delane as a potential trade-up target like Bain could be. Bain's window could legitimately start at No. 4 overall and I can't see him getting past No. 9, while Delane's window starts at No. 8 and probably goes down to No. 12, unless the Cowboys are one of those McCoy teams. The Seahawks declined to franchise tag or re-sign Kenneth Walker III after he rushed for 135 yards in Seattle's 29-13 Super Bowl win over the Patriots. Whether it's with the final pick in the first round or by trading back, White expects Seattle to prioritize a replacement. "No. 32 might be a little high for Jadarian Price, but I think there's a good chance the Seahawks are taking him with their first pick in a different spot," White said. "Running back is their clearest need with Kenneth Walker gone and Zach Charbonnet injured, and we saw how big an impact the rushing attack had in the Super Bowl last year. Seattle has just four picks and will likely prioritize adding more on Draft Day, and those late first-round picks are key for those looking to trade up (maybe for Ty Simpson?) as they come with a fifth-year option. He and CJ Allen play a non-premium position at off-ball linebacker but have high floors and reasons to believe each could land in Round 1, especially to teams looking for a piece to come in and make an immediate impact. Rodriguez won a lot of hardware for his collegiate performance in 2025, and in particular, I could see a number of teams in the back half of Round 1 having him higher on their boards than we expect. Lions draft safety first (+3000) Brad Holmes is a best-player-available type of drafter, and with offensive lineman a massive -380 favorite in this prop, I see potential to take a big swing on a lottery ticket play.
